# OpenFocus art guide

This folder holds the pixel-art pipeline: the shared palette, credits, editable sources and tools.
**All art in the app today is placeholder** (CC0, generated by `tools/build_placeholders.py`).
Real art is very welcome. This guide explains how to make art that fits.

## Style rules
| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Palette | [`palette.hex`](palette.hex) / [`palette.gpl`](palette.gpl). Stay inside it, and open an issue if you need a colour that isn't there. |
| Characters | 32×32 frames; the hero stands on row 30 with the head starting near row 6 |
| Props / small icons | 16×16 |
| Achievement badges | 24×24 |
| Goal mountain scene | 160×112 |
| Backdrops | 48×48, round with a 1px outline; the hero stands at offset (8, 13) |
| Launcher icon | 54×54 canvas (scales ×2/×3/×4/×6/×8 to every density) |
| Outline | 1px, colour `#2b2440` ("outline"), not pure black, so it works on light and dark themes |
| Lighting | light from the top-left; 3-step ramps (light / mid / dark) |
| Anti-aliasing | none; no semi-transparent pixels |

## Sprite sheets
Cosmetics and their slots are defined in `content.json` (see the [content editor](../tools/content-editor/README.md)), which references sprites by file name. After adding or resizing any `px_*.png`, run the generator. It regenerates `ui/pixel/SpriteRegistry.kt`, and a test fails if the registry is stale.

- Sheets are **fixed grids**: one row per animation, frames left to right, no padding.
- Export as **PNG to `app/src/main/res/drawable-nodpi/`**. The `-nodpi` folder stops Android from resizing the image.
- Name files `px_<thing>.png`. Cosmetics use their shop id, e.g. `hat_wizard` becomes `px_hat_wizard.png`.
- Register the sheet in `app/src/main/java/org/openfocus/app/ui/pixel/SpriteCatalog.kt` with its frame size, its animations (`row`, `frames`, `fps`) and any anchors.

### The hero, a layered "paper doll"
The hero is drawn as layers, bottom to top:
1. `px_bg_<id>.png`: round 48×48 backdrop (`px_bg_default.png` when none is equipped)
2. `px_hero_body_<tone>.png`: skin, hair, outline and boots, one sheet per skin tone (`light`, `medium`, `deep`)
3. `px_cloak_<colour>.png`: the cloak pixels only
4. `px_armour_<id>.png`: a single-frame overlay that follows the `body` anchor (it hops with the celebrate jump)
5. `px_hat_<id>.png`: a single-frame overlay that follows the `head` anchor

The order comes from each slot's `layer` in `content.json`. New slots slot in automatically.

Layers 2–4 are 32×32 and sit at offset (8, 13) inside the backdrop. Each layer animates at its own fps (for example the night sky twinkles at 1.5 fps while the hero idles at 3 fps). All loops should divide evenly into the renderer's 12-second clock.

Body and cloak sheets share this layout:

| Row | Animation | Frames | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `idle` | 4 @ 3 fps | frame 1 = head down 1px, frame 3 = blink |
| 1 | `rest` | 1 | eyes closed, head down 1px (shown when HP runs out) |
| 2 | `celebrate` | 2 @ 4 fps | arms raised; frame 1 jumps up 1px (level-ups, achievements) |

**Hats** are drawn against the head in idle frame 0. The renderer moves them by the body's `head` anchor on each frame, so a hat bobs with the head without needing its own animation. If you change the body animation, update `HEAD_BOB` in `SpriteCatalog.kt` (and `IDLE_BOB` in the generator).

### Goal ascent
`px_ascent_<colorIndex>.png` is 160×224: row 0 is the climbing scene, row 1 the summit-reached scene. The dashed trail is baked into the art. Its waypoints are listed in **both** `TRAIL` in the generator and `AscentTrail.POINTS` in Kotlin, and a test checks that every waypoint lands on the mountain rather than the sky. If you redraw the mountain, update both lists.

| Sheet | Frame | Rows | Placement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `px_tent.png` | 8×8 | `unlit` (1), `lit` (2 @ 3 fps) | feet at (4, 6); camp *i* of *n* sits at (i+1)/(n+1) along the trail |
| `px_climber.png` | 10×12 | `idle` (2 @ 2 fps) | feet at (5, 11), 7px left of the camp it has reached |
| `px_flag.png` | 8×8 | `red`, `gold` (2 @ 3 fps each) | pole base on the peak at (88, 10) |

The detail screen stretches the scene to fill its width (`integerScale = false`). Thumbnails keep whole-number scaling.

### Achievement badges
`px_badges.png` is an atlas of 24×24 medals, 5 per row, in the same order as the achievements in `content.json`. Each badge's animation name is the achievement id, and its position comes from `SpriteAnim.col`/`row`. A medal is a tier disc (bronze, silver or gold, with a lit top-left rim) on purple ribbon tails, with a 12×12 symbol centred at (6, 4). Locked badges aren't drawn separately: the app tints the unlocked art into a flat silhouette.

To add an achievement, use the [content editor](../tools/content-editor/README.md). The generator reads the order and tiers straight from `content.json`. To give the achievement its own symbol, add a 12×12 grid to `GLYPHS`, keyed by the achievement id; until then it gets a star.

`px_sparkle.png` (48×48, 8 frames at 10 fps) is drawn over the 48px hero avatar in the level-up and achievement dialog. It's the same logical size, so both snap to the same pixel scale.

### Other sheets
| Sheet | Frame | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `px_shield.png` | 48×48 × 4 @ 1 fps | Block screen and onboarding; the glow cycle lasts one 4 s breath |
| `px_empty.png` | 64×48 atlas: `today`, `habits`, `goals` | `EmptyState(scene = …)`; order must match `EMPTY_SCENES` |

### Launcher icon
The icon is drawn on a 54×54 canvas and exported at ×2/×3/×4/×6/×8 to `mipmap-*/ic_launcher_fg.png`, with a white `ic_launcher_mono.png` for Android 13+ themed icons. Keep content inside the central 36×36 (the adaptive-icon safe zone); the background is `@color/launcher_background`. `art/export/ic_launcher_store.png` (486 px, 54×9) is ready for store listings; pad it to 512 if a store requires that size. The notification icon is still the vector `drawable/ic_launcher_foreground.xml`.

### Light and dark themes
Sprites are drawn once and must read on both the light (`#F7F4FF`) and dark (`#14121F`) backgrounds:
- Big scenes that fill a card get a **night row**: `climbing_night` / `summit_night` for each ascent, and `night` for the default backdrop. The app picks the night row when the theme background is dark.
- Ground shadows use translucent palette entries (`_` and `=` in the generator, written as `RRGGBBAA`) so they darken whatever is underneath instead of glowing.
- Check `docs/screenshots/dark/` (from `DarkScreenshotTest`) whenever you add art.

### Rendering
`PixelSprite` draws with nearest-neighbour filtering and rounds the scale down to a whole number, so every source pixel becomes an equal square block of screen pixels. Animations stop when the user has turned off system animations.

## Workflow
1. Draw in [Pixelorama](https://orama-interactive.itch.io/pixelorama) (MIT), [LibreSprite](https://libresprite.github.io/) (GPL), or any editor that exports PNG sprite sheets. Load `palette.gpl` first.
2. Put the editable source file (`.pxo`, `.ase`, `.aseprite` or a layered `.png`) in `art/src/`.
3. Export the PNG sheet into `drawable-nodpi/` and register it in `SpriteCatalog.kt`.
4. If you are replacing a generated placeholder, delete its entry in `tools/build_placeholders.py` so it isn't overwritten.
5. Add a line to [`CREDITS.md`](CREDITS.md).
6. Run `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest`. It checks sheet dimensions and that every shop item has art, and regenerates `docs/screenshots/sprites.png` so reviewers can see your work.

If a cosmetic has no sprite yet, the app falls back to the old shape-drawn hero. Art can land one piece at a time.

## Licensing
Accepted: **CC0, CC-BY 3.0/4.0, CC-BY-SA 3.0/4.0, GPL-3.0-compatible**.
Not accepted: anything **NonCommercial (NC)** or **NoDerivatives (ND)** (this rules out, for example, Habitica's sprites), or art copied or traced from other games.
Every file must be listed in `CREDITS.md`.

## Roadmap
- [x] Phase 1: renderer, palette, pipeline, placeholder hero, hats and coin
- [x] Phase 2: 3 skin tones (stored in the profile, DB v2), pixel backdrops, celebrate animation. Placeholder quality: hand-drawn replacements welcome.
- [x] Phase 3: goal mountain scene: one 160×112 sheet per goal colour (climbing / summit rows), tents (unlit / lit flicker), climber, flag (red / gold)
- [x] Phase 4: 20 achievement medals (bronze / silver / gold), locked silhouettes, level-up sparkle burst, coin in reward snackbars
- [x] Phase 5: breathing block-screen shield, empty-state scenes (today / habits / goals), onboarding art, pixel launcher icon (+ monochrome + 486px store export)
- [x] Phase 6: dark-theme pass: night versions of every goal scene and of the default backdrop, translucent ground shadows, dark screenshots in `docs/screenshots/dark/`, a test that every loop divides the 12 s clock
- [ ] Next: replace the placeholders with hand-drawn art and review on real devices (contributors welcome!)
